comment: LeCrone is difficult and gives a lot of work. With that being said, his office hours are absolutely wonderful, and he works very hard to genuinely help his students. Hardest class I've taken at UR. However, it pushed me in a way that made me truly understand the material and helped me grow as a student. If you love math or learning, take LeCrone.

Not great. Be ready to review notes and textbook twelve times and still get points off on quizzes and exams for miniscule wording issues. No answer keys to homework, so you never know you're doing things wrong until you take a quiz. Talks way too fast in lectures. His sandpile grading system makes it possible to pass though.
Too hard. One kid used chat gpt and he crashed out and made the class exponentially more difficult afterwards.

Unique grading system so that it's possible to pass, but you need to go above and beyond for an A. He has an upbeat personality and makes lectures interesting. He is super accessible outside of class and has frequent office hours. Great at explaining

Dr. Lecrone is very enthusiastic about math and is always accessible for extra help. With that said, his lectures are hard to follow (just read the textbook), he isn't great at answering questions, and he can be condescending at times. He makes it easy to pass the class with the sandpile grading system, but getting an A is no easy feat.

This was one of the most difficult courses I have taken to date. A lot of it was due to the textbook that he chose. If you do the work, it should not be super difficult to get a good grade, as the sandpile grading system adds a lot of buffer. However, just know that this course takes a lot of time and you will have work hard to do well.

Dr. LeCrone is probably the most difficult math prof I've ever taken, but he's also probably the best. It is hard to do well in this class, but if you put in the work, Dr. LeCrone will help you succeed. You will leave this class better at math.

Dr LeCrone is so smart and so passionate. He's kind and easy to talk to and always available to help. There is so much homework for this class. I spent 12-15+ hours a week on this class. He has specific criteria for your work and grades very harshly. You will learn a lot but he will not make it easy. Be prepared to be buried in math work.

Overall Dr. LeCrone is a brilliant, and passionate professor. He challenges his students every day, and the material of his class is quite rigorous, which leads to a comprehensive understanding by the end. Dr. LeCrone's teaching is not for students trying to earn an easy A, but it is for the students who want to reach higher levels of mathematics.

The most inspirational Math prof at UoR! Extremely knowledgeable, engaging, always there to help. Amount of workload is fair for Calc 3. He is a fair grader, but his exams are challenging. If you love playing with Math, he is the best to ignite your interest, but it is in no planet an easy A or even B. Highly recommend if you want to learn Math!
Best math professor I've ever had, enthusiastic and funny guy, great at explaining concepts, 50% of the grade was based on 4 exams, the other 50% was on homeworks and participation

He made this course harder than it should have been. True, he's enthusiastic about math, but this is too much for me, a student who doesn't like math. His course simply made my whole semester stressful. He didn't show empathy for students who were not smart enough, because he thought you did not practice enough.

He's so enthusiastic about math that sometimes he actually talks too fast during lectures. He knows this is a hard subject so he gives many fluff points where even if you average C- on tests you can end with a B+. Strict with taking points off on tests though so you really gotta study

Dr. LeCrone structures his classes as a mix of homework problem presentations by students and then lectures afterwards. His lectures are fantastic when he's not rushing, and the homework presentations are great for correcting mistakes in your approach to problems. Exams are take-homes with an oral portion. One of the best math professors to take.

I love this man! I can't believe someone giving him anything lower than a 5, unless you hate math-which really shouldn't be the attitude to study anything... Also I want to say that he is extremely funny in a nerdy way, but all in all, he is the kind of professor that has the deterministic effect on major decisions/future plans etc.

He is very passionate and explains things very thoroughly. He keeps things engaging too and there are a lot of opportunities to improve your grade in the class besides the exams. The opportunities really incentivize you to do the work outside of class, and there are so many that it makes it okay if you have "bad days" and don't do all the work.

Dr. LeCrone is a very organized professor. He emphasizes the logical flow of math proofs, which has helped me understand problems better. His lectures and grading are clear. He incorporates reflection, goal setting, and opportunities to ask questions and interact with peers into his classroom. This is the second class I've taken with him.

Dr. LeCrone is a pretty solid professor as far as teaching goes, but his grading system makes it so that you can pick and choose which assignments fit you best and still get a great grade. The oral exams (easier than they sound) are still somewhat tough but don't account for that much of your grade. Reading the sections before class helps a lot.

I think depending on how you take LeCrone's class, it can be very easy or very hard. I personally barely did the textbook work except for what he expected quickly before class, barely read the textbook, and did fine in the class. He also has many opportunities for you to do work to succeed, if you work hard you're pretty much guaranteed an A.

He is passionate about mathematics and is very nice. But, he didnt show the basic empathy needed for students during the COVID crisis that I got from every other professor. I learned a lot and did well. He just made it unnecessarily stressful. To me, he cared more about his career as a professor than actually putting himself in our shoes.

Dr. LeCrone gets a bad rap but mostly because of the course he teaches. Calculus II is nationally one of the most failed college courses. However, he makes it easy to pass. 60% of your grade is based on homework, participation, and quizzes. Also, you don't need to do all of your homework to get the full 60%. This class is definitely passable.
Dr. LeCrone is awesome, people are just scared of thinking.

Could only pick 3 tags but would also add Respected, Accessible Outside Class, Caring. Also pretty funny. Amazing prof and a really cool guy. All his classes are tough from what I've heard, but his grading policy rewards hard work so your fate's in your own hands. Really a master of what he teaches and much more engaging than most other professors.
This was the worst class i've ever taken.

The worst teacher I have ever had. He is rigid, inconsistent in the way he grades, and his expectations of what his students should know far exceeds what he should expect based on the quality of his teaching. I had already learned and understood the material in the first unit, but no longer understood and got a 54% on the test. I hate math now.

Good professor, excellent chapter explanations during class. However, he expects you to read the chapter, understand it and do the homework before class which is unreasonable and frustrating sometimes.

Possibly the worst class I've ever had. Walked into the semester absolutely loving math and calculus, and now I'm leaving happy to never take another math class again. Looking back at tests, I have no idea why 10+ points were taken off for problems when the answer was right. You're better off taking it online. Self-taught either way.
Great guy. Horrible professor. He uses big words and makes everything 10x harder than it needs to be.
Challenging course, but Dr. LeCrone explains the material well and in depth. Homework was largely optional and was time-consuming, but it offered (needed) preparation for exams.

Dr. LeCrone is in general a nice guy, but not the best professor. He will have you read  each chapter before class and then go over it really generally, not nearly enough for his near impossible grading standards. A lot of homework and comes off as arrogant. He does know what he's talking about, but he also assumes the class does too.

Awful! Did not teach at all in class. He simply read definitions from the book for class and expected us to figure out the rest. His grading was extremely inconsistent and the homework assignments took forever. He will give you  some easy extra points but it does not make up for his inability to teach. He also comes across as rude and arrogant.

Super passionate about his topic. His enthusiasm is contagious. Do your homework on WebAssign, create a plan for earning points. Weekly hws are time consuming and hyped up versions of daily hw, but really helpful. Tons of extra credit, although he does such a good job explaining things and is so accessible outside of class that you hardly need it.
